# ZOZI Backend — Feature-to-Feature & Module-to-Module Architecture Audit

*Generated by `scripts/coherence_gate.py` + `scripts/audit_features.py`. Re-run after changes.*

## 1. Scope & Method

Audited the FastAPI backend (flat layout: `routers/`, `controllers/`, `services/`,
`models/`, plus `db/`, `providers/`, `middleware/`, `events/`, `jobs/`, `utils/`,
`dependencies/`, `scripts/`).

Two graphs were built:

* **Module-to-module (layered):** the four application layers
  `routers(0) → controllers(1) → services(2) → models(3) → providers(4)`,
  with `models` as a **leaf**. The contract is *unidirectional downward only*.
* **Feature-to-feature:** canonical feature domains = sub-packages under
  `controllers/`, `services/`, `models/` (e.g. `commerce`, `orders`, `finance`,
  `supplier`). Routers are flat/encoded and were mapped to a feature by the
  domain sub-packages they import.

Totals: **205 routers, 156 controllers, 460 services, 42 model modules**,
66 utils, 57 providers, 20 middleware, 13 db, 6 jobs, 2 events.

---

## 2. Module-to-Module Layered Coherence

### 2.1 Internal import-flow (top edges, deduplicated module→module)

| Edge | Count | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| services → models | 2263 | ✅ allowed |
| controllers → services | 1618 | ✅ allowed |
| services → services | 1009 | ✅ allowed (composition) |
| routers → controllers | 522 | ✅ allowed |
| routers → services | 513 | ✅ allowed |
| **services → controllers** | **255 raw / 57 unique** | ❌ **hard violation** |
| controllers → routers | 98 raw / 3 unique | ⚠️ soft (facade re-export) |
| services → routers | 4 | ❌ hard violation (in `extracted`) |
| models → models / db / utils | — | ✅ allowed (leaf ≠ upward) |

### 2.2 Directional violations (authoritative)

* **57 hard violations** — *every one* is inside **`services.extracted.*`**
  importing a controller or router. Examples:
  * `services.extracted.system_ai_upload_service` → `controllers.admin.admin_controller`
  * `services.extracted.logistics_logistics_status_service` → `controllers.orders.logistics_controller`, `routers.core_auth_routes`
  * `services.extracted.governance_package_service` → `controllers.security.auth_controller`
* **~32 soft violations** (controllers → routers), not 3 as earlier reported:
  * **3** controllers re-export router packages
    (`governance.compliance_controller`, `finance.expense_controller`,
    `governance.operational_controller` → `routers.governance_package` /
    `routers.finance_package`).
  * **29** controllers import the generated helper
    `routers.generated.auto_router` (a separate upward-coupling locus that the
    first pass under-reported). Acceptable as facades, but counted here.

**Key finding:** The layering contract is otherwise intact. The *only* real
**hard** breach locus is the `services/extracted/` package (54 modules). No
service outside `extracted` imports a controller or router. The **soft**
breach locus is `controllers → routers` (3 re-exports + 29 `auto_router`
imports).

## 4. Feature-to-Feature Coupling

Out-degree = number of *other* feature domains a feature's modules import.
High out-degree = low encapsulation (a "god" feature).

| Feature | Out-degree | Imports (sample) |
|---|---:|---|
| extracted | 91 | almost everything (violating) |
| finance | 83 | orders, treasury, supplier, logistics, erp, customer, employee_models… |
| admin | 81 | commerce, products, treasury, security, comms, gateways, geography… |
| treasury | 66 | finance, payments, gateways, logistics, supplier, orders… |
| users | 66 | security, hierarchy, comms, customer, admin… |
| customer | 65 | commerce, security, comms, orders, products… |
| security | 51 | permissions, customer, hr, logistics, fraud… |
| comms | 43 | marketing, incident, hr, fraud, user, logistics… |
| supplier | 43 | finance, logistics, products, geography, treasury, ai… |
| common | 42 | finance, treasury, comms, erp, media_models… |
| orders | 42 | commerce, logistics, finance, treasury, gateways, products… |
| ai | 40 | finance, treasury, gateways, comms… |
| logistics | 36 | geography, treasury, finance, country_enhancements… |
| geography | 33 | countries, treasury, supplier, finance, logistics… |
| commerce | 30 | orders, products, promotions, payments, comms, logistics… |
| delegators | 25 | all 25 domain features (facade) |

**Finding:** the domain features are *deeply* cross-wired. `finance`, `admin`,
`treasury`, `users`, `customer` each reach 60–80 other domains. There are **no
bounded contexts** — e.g. `finance` touches `employee_models`, `marketing`,
`fraud`, `incident` etc. This is the natural result of a single shared
`models.*` namespace with no per-feature encapsulation. It is not a *contract*
violation, but it is a **maintainability / change-risk** gap.

*Isolated / leaf features (low coupling, mostly engines):* `analytics` (7),
`system` (8), `core` (9), `mcp` (1), `location_service` (2), `hierarchy` (2).

## 5. Gap Analysis — what is missing / what to add

### 5.1 (P0) Dissolve `services/extracted/` — the only real contract breach
54 service modules live in a package that violates the DIP by importing
controllers/routers (57 hard violations). **What to add/fix:**
* Move each `extracted` service into its proper domain package
  (`services.finance`, `services.orders`, `services.security`, …) **or** delete
  it if it duplicates an existing service.
* Replace any `service → controller` call with `service → service` (call the
  underlying service, not the HTTP-facing controller).
* Add a CI gate (`pytest` over `coherence_gate`) to fail the build if
  `services` ever imports `controllers`/`routers` again.

### 5.2 (P0/P1) Genuine orphan model modules — verified

> **Correction (post-verification):** the earlier draft used a *subpackage-only*
> grouping, which falsely flagged `fraud`/`commission`/`permissions` as orphans
> because their services live in `services/security/*` and `services/finance/*`.
> A name-based, cross-layer pass (now the default in `scripts/audit_features.py`)
> shows those three are **fully backed**. The real orphan set is small.

A model module is "orphan" only if **no service or controller anywhere**
references it by name. The verified orphans:

* **`marketing`** — `models/marketing.py` (2 classes) with **no service,
  controller, or router**. The only true end-to-end orphan.
  → Either implement `services/marketing/` + `controllers/marketing/` or delete
  the dead model.
* **`countries`, `country_control`, `country_enhancements`** — geography
  sub-models. Referenced by `geography` at runtime but no owning
  `services/geography` import recorded. → Confirm `services/geography` imports
  them, or fold into `models/geography`.
* **`media_models`, `mixins`** — base/abstract models (`mixins`:
  `TenantMixin`, `SoftDeleteMixin`, `AuditMixin`). Intentionally used via
  subclassing. Keep; document as base-only.

**NOT orphans (corrected):**
* `fraud` → `models/fraud.py` + `routers/fraud_detection.py` + 5
  `services/security/fraud_*.py` + 2 controllers in `delegators`. Backed.
* `commission` → `models/commission.py` + 2 routers + 5
  `services/finance/commission_*.py` + `controllers/finance/commission_controller.py`. Backed.
* `permissions` → `models/permissions/*` + 3 controllers + services scattered
  across `security`/`admin`/`hr` (2 of those — `admin_permissions_validation_service`,
  `public_permissions_validation_service` — live in `services/extracted/` and are
  absorbed by §5.1). Backed, but fragmented; consolidate into `services/security`
  after the `extracted` dissolution.

### 5.3 (P1) Backed features missing an HTTP controller

These have a **model + service but no controller** — reachable internally
(service-to-service) but exposing no HTTP surface. Decide per feature: add a
controller (if externally reachable) or mark internal-only.

* **`onboarding`** — model + 2 services (`supplier`/`security` onboarding),
  **0 controllers**. The supplier KYC flow most likely needs a
  `controllers/onboarding/`. → add controller.
* `fraud`, `incident`, `payments`, `promotions`, `employee`, `erp`,
  `upload_job`, `user` — same pattern (model+svc, no ctrl). Most
  (`erp`, `upload_job`, `user`) are internal/workflow services that may
  legitimately stay controller-less; `fraud`/`payments`/`incident` should get
  controllers if they serve external API clients.

### 5.4 (P1) `delegators` — 94 controllers, 0 services — review for dead weight
These are documented as facade/composition shims. Per the earlier analysis
they are *not dead*, but 94 is large. **What to add:** an explicit test/
registry asserting each delegator composes ≥1 real controller, so future
"empty" delegators are caught. Flag any delegator whose body only re-exports a
single sibling controller (candidate for deletion).

### 5.5 (P2) Weak encapsulation / no bounded contexts
The 12 most-coupled features each reach 25–91 other domains through a single
shared `models.*` namespace. **What to add:**
* Introduce per-feature **schema/API boundaries** (each feature exposes a
  service interface; cross-feature calls go through that interface, not raw
  model access).
* Consider splitting `models` into per-domain schema packages so a feature
  cannot accidentally import another's internals.
* Add an architecture test asserting a max fan-out per feature (e.g. ≤ N
  cross-feature imports) to keep the graph from regressing.

### 5.6 (P2) Router→feature mapping gaps (74/205 unmapped)
74 routers import only generic modules (`fastapi`, `db`, `utils`,
`dependencies`) and resolve their targets at runtime, so the audit couldn't
auto-assign them a feature. **What to add:** a `routers/*/__init__` or a
registry mapping each router module → owning feature, so the audit (and future
owners) can validate "every router has a backing feature."

## 6. Prioritized Backlog

| Pri | Action | Effort | Risk if ignored |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | Dissolve `services.extracted` (54 modules / 57 violations; includes `admin_permissions_validation_service`, `public_permissions_validation_service`) | M | Contract keeps breaking; tests can't trust layering |
| P0 | Resolve genuine orphan `marketing` (model only — no svc/ctrl/rtr): implement or delete | S | Dead model; confuses owners |
| P1 | Confirm/fold geography sub-models (`countries`, `country_control`, `country_enhancements`) into `services/geography` | S | Orphaned models drift |
| P1 | Add `controllers/onboarding/` (model + services exist, no controller) | S | Supplier KYC flow has no HTTP surface |
| P1 | Add controllers for externally-reachable backed features (`fraud`, `payments`, `incident`) where needed; mark `erp`/`upload_job`/`user` internal-only | M | Inconsistent HTTP surface |
| P1 | Consolidate fragmented `permissions` services into `services/security` post-extracted dissolution | S | Logic scattered / duplicated |
| P1 | Audit `delegators` (94) for empties | S | Hidden dead code |
| P2 | Introduce bounded contexts + fan-out test (current max: `extracted` 91, `finance`/`admin`/`treasury`/`users` 60–80) | L | Change risk grows unbounded |
| P2 | Router→feature registry for the 74 unmapped routers (3 re-exports + 29 `auto_router` imports are the soft-coupling locus) | S | Audit blind spots |
